severity_rationale: Disabling authentication for RPC clients could lead to accidental information disclosure, but requires an underlying RPC service vulnerability to be exploited.

rule_title: 18.9.38.2 Ensure 'Restrict Unauthenticated RPC clients' is set to 'Enabled: Authenticated'
failure_scenario: Unauthenticated RPC clients can connect to local RPC servers, potentially enabling remote code execution or privilege escalation.
severity_rationale: Unauthenticated RPC connections allow arbitrary network attackers to execute code or escalate privileges on the local system.

rule_title: 18.9.4.1 Ensure 'Encryption Oracle Remediation' is set to 'Enabled: Force Updated Clients'
failure_scenario: An attacker exploits the CredSSP encryption oracle vulnerability to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable workstation.
severity_rationale: This vulnerability allows remote code execution on unpatched systems, with no user interaction or privileges required.

rule_title: 18.9.4.2 Ensure 'Remote host allows delegation of non-exportable credentials' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker on a remote host can steal credentials delegated to the host, potentially gaining unauthorized access to other systems.
severity_rationale: Credential delegation enables cross-system compromise if an attacker gains access to a remote host with delegated credentials.

rule_title: 18.9.53.1.1 Ensure 'Enable Windows NTP Client' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: The system clock drifts out of sync with authoritative time sources, potentially causing authentication failures, log timestamp inconsistencies, and distributed application errors.
severity_rationale: Time synchronization failures primarily affect system integrity and availability of time-sensitive services, but do not directly grant attacker access.

rule_title: 18.9.7.2 Ensure 'Prevent automatic download of applications associated with device metadata' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Third-party utility software associated with hardware devices is automatically installed under the SYSTEM account, potentially creating backdoors or vulnerabilities.
severity_rationale: While not directly granting remote access, this setting prevents proper software installation controls and could allow unauthorized SYSTEM-level software installation.

rule_title: 19.5.1.1 Ensure 'Turn off toast notifications on the lock screen' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Sensitive application notifications may be displayed on the lock screen while the system is unattended, potentially exposing confidential information.
severity_rationale: Physical attackers can observe sensitive data displayed on the lock screen without authentication.

rule_title: 19.7.26.1 Ensure 'Prevent users from sharing files within their profile.' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A user accidentally shares sensitive files from their profile with unauthorized network users, potentially exposing confidential data.
severity_rationale: While not directly enabling exploitation, this setting prevents accidental exposure of sensitive data to unauthorized users on the local network.

rule_title: 19.7.5.1 Ensure 'Do not preserve zone information in file attachments' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Users are not warned about potentially malicious files downloaded from untrusted sources, increasing the risk of execution of malicious code.
severity_rationale: Disabling zone information preservation removes a critical security feature that warns users about potentially dangerous files, making it easier for users to execute malicious code.

rule_title: 19.7.5.2 Ensure 'Notify antivirus programs when opening attachments' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Downloaded files are not scanned by registered antivirus programs, potentially allowing malicious attachments to execute without detection.
severity_rationale: Disabling this setting allows malicious attachments to bypass antivirus scanning, potentially leading to full system compromise.

rule_title: 19.7.8.1 Ensure 'Configure Windows spotlight on lock screen' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Windows Spotlight collects and transmits user data to Microsoft, potentially exposing sensitive information to third parties.
severity_rationale: Enabling Windows Spotlight creates a data leakage vector by transmitting user activity and system information to Microsoft.

rule_title: 19.7.8.2 Ensure 'Do not suggest third-party content in Windows spotlight' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Windows Spotlight collects and shares user data with third-party software publishers, potentially exposing user browsing history and preferences.
severity_rationale: Data sharing with third parties may expose user activity patterns, but does not directly enable system compromise or service disruption.

rule_title: 19.7.8.5 Ensure 'Turn off Spotlight collection on Desktop' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: The system automatically downloads and displays Microsoft-provided desktop wallpapers, potentially sharing user browsing history and system information with Microsoft.
severity_rationale: While this does not directly grant attacker access, it represents a privacy concern where user data may be shared with third parties.

rule_title: 2.2.1 Ensure 'Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller' is set to 'No One'
failure_scenario: A malicious application running under a compromised user account could access and exfiltrate other users' saved credentials from Credential Manager.
severity_rationale: This setting protects stored credentials from unauthorized access by applications running under standard user accounts.

rule_title: 2.2.10 Ensure 'Create a token object' is set to 'No One'
failure_scenario: A local user with the 'Create a token object' privilege can create an elevated access token, potentially allowing privilege escalation or denial of service.
severity_rationale: This sensitive privilege allows local users to manipulate system access tokens, potentially leading to full system compromise or denial of service.

rule_title: 2.2.11 Ensure 'Create global objects' is set to 'Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE'
failure_scenario: An authenticated local user can create global objects that may interfere with system services or processes running under other accounts, potentially causing application failures or data corruption.
severity_rationale: This is a defense-in-depth control that prevents local users from creating global objects that could interfere with system services, but does not directly enable privilege escalation or data compromise.

rule_title: 2.2.12 Ensure 'Create permanent shared objects' is set to 'No One'
failure_scenario: A local attacker with low privileges can create shared objects that expose sensitive data to the network, potentially leaking system information.
severity_rationale: Low-privileged local users can create shared objects that expose sensitive data to the network, creating a confidentiality impact.

rule_title: 2.2.13 Ensure 'Create symbolic links' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: A local user creates malicious symbolic links that manipulate file permissions, corrupt data, or cause denial-of-service conditions.
severity_rationale: Symbolic link manipulation can cause data corruption, permission changes, or service disruptions, but requires an underlying application vulnerability to be exploited.

rule_title: 2.2.14 Ensure 'Debug programs' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: A local unprivileged user can attach a debugger to arbitrary processes, potentially extracting sensitive information or injecting malicious code.
severity_rationale: Debugging privileges allow process memory inspection and modification, which could be exploited to extract sensitive data or inject malicious code, but requires an existing local user account.

rule_title: 2.2.15 Ensure 'Deny access to this computer from the network' to include 'Guests'
failure_scenario: Remote unauthenticated or untrusted guest users can enumerate network resources and access shared files, potentially disclosing sensitive information.
severity_rationale: Permitting network guest access enables information disclosure through network resource enumeration and file sharing.

rule_title: 2.2.16 Ensure 'Deny log on as a batch job' to include 'Guests'
failure_scenario: Unauthenticated guest accounts can schedule and execute batch jobs, potentially consuming excessive system resources and causing denial of service.
severity_rationale: Guest accounts can be used to schedule resource-intensive jobs, potentially causing system availability degradation.

rule_title: 2.2.17 Ensure 'Deny log on as a service' to include 'Guests'
failure_scenario: A guest user can register and run unauthorized services with SYSTEM privileges, potentially enabling privilege escalation or malicious payload execution.
severity_rationale: While guest users cannot directly install services, they can register and run them with SYSTEM privileges if the service is configured to do so, potentially enabling privilege escalation or malicious payload execution.

rule_title: 2.2.18 Ensure 'Deny log on locally' to include 'Guests'
failure_scenario: Unauthenticated or untrusted guest users can log on locally to the system console, gaining unauthorized interactive access.
severity_rationale: Permitting local guest logon grants interactive access to arbitrary local users with no privileges required, creating full system compromise potential.

rule_title: 2.2.19 Ensure 'Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services' to include 'Guests'
failure_scenario: Remote unauthenticated or untrusted guest users can establish Remote Desktop sessions to the host, gaining unauthorized interactive access.
severity_rationale: Permitting network guest logon grants interactive access to arbitrary network users with no privileges required, creating full system compromise potential.

rule_title: 2.2.2 Ensure 'Access this computer from the network' is set to 'Administrators, Remote Desktop Users'
failure_scenario: Unauthorized network users can access shared resources on the host system, potentially gaining access to sensitive data or executing malicious code.
severity_rationale: Network access to shared resources is enabled by default, creating a potential attack surface for unauthorized access to sensitive data and system compromise.

rule_title: 2.2.20 Ensure 'Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation' is set to 'No One'
failure_scenario: An attacker with administrative privileges can enable delegation for arbitrary accounts, allowing them to impersonate other users and access network resources.
severity_rationale: Privileged attackers can enable delegation to gain unauthorized access to network resources and compromise system integrity.

rule_title: 2.2.21 Ensure 'Force shutdown from a remote system' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: An authenticated low-privileged user can remotely shut down the system, causing a denial-of-service condition.
severity_rationale: Network-available shutdown capability creates a denial-of-service vector for authenticated low-privileged users.

rule_title: 2.2.22 Ensure 'Generate security audits' is set to 'LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE'
failure_scenario: An attacker with local system access can generate excessive audit events, potentially overwriting legitimate security logs and obscuring malicious activity.
severity_rationale: While not directly granting access, this control weakens audit integrity by allowing local system accounts to generate excessive logs that could obscure security events.

rule_title: 2.2.23 Ensure 'Impersonate a client after authentication' is set to 'Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE'
failure_scenario: An attacker with local user privileges can create a malicious service that impersonates authenticated users connecting to it, potentially elevating their privileges to administrative or system levels.
severity_rationale: This sensitive privilege allows privilege escalation through token impersonation, but requires an attacker to create a service and trick a client to connect to it.

rule_title: 2.2.24 Ensure 'Increase scheduling priority' is set to 'Administrators, Window Manager\Window Manager Group'
failure_scenario: A non-administrator user can increase the scheduling priority of a process to Real-Time, causing system performance degradation or denial of service.
severity_rationale: Non-administrator users can cause system-wide availability degradation by increasing process priority.

rule_title: 2.2.25 Ensure 'Load and unload device drivers' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: A local user installs a malicious device driver, gaining elevated system privileges and compromising the entire host.
severity_rationale: Local users can load arbitrary drivers with administrative privileges, enabling full system compromise.

rule_title: 2.2.26 Ensure 'Lock pages in memory' is set to 'No One'
failure_scenario: A local user with the Lock pages in memory privilege can allocate excessive physical memory to processes, causing system performance degradation or denial of service.
severity_rationale: This is a resource exhaustion vulnerability requiring only a standard user account and no special conditions.

rule_title: 2.2.29 Ensure 'Manage auditing and security log' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: Non-administrator users can clear the Security event log, erasing evidence of unauthorized activity and compromising forensic investigation.
severity_rationale: Log tampering weakens the integrity of audit trails and forensic evidence, but requires an authenticated local user account.

rule_title: 2.2.3 Ensure 'Act as part of the operating system' is set to 'No One'
failure_scenario: An attacker with local access can exploit a vulnerable application to gain SYSTEM privileges and fully compromise the host.
severity_rationale: This sensitive privilege allows local privilege escalation to SYSTEM, which is the highest privilege level on Windows systems.

rule_title: 2.2.30 Ensure 'Modify an object label' is set to 'No One'
failure_scenario: A local user can modify the integrity label of files or processes owned by other users, potentially causing them to execute code at higher privilege levels.
severity_rationale: Local users can escalate the integrity level of other users' processes, potentially enabling privilege escalation attacks.

rule_title: 2.2.31 Ensure 'Modify firmware environment values' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: An unprivileged local user can modify firmware environment values, potentially causing hardware misconfiguration and system instability.
severity_rationale: While not directly granting system compromise, this control prevents unauthorized hardware misconfiguration that could lead to minor system instability.

rule_title: 2.2.32 Ensure 'Perform volume maintenance tasks' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: A local user can delete a volume, causing data loss and availability degradation.
severity_rationale: Local users can delete volumes, causing data loss and availability degradation.

rule_title: 2.2.33 Ensure 'Profile single process' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: Non-administrator users can use performance monitoring tools to identify critical processes and other security controls, aiding targeted attacks.
severity_rationale: This control limits information disclosure about system processes and security controls to authorized users only.

rule_title: 2.2.34 Ensure 'Profile system performance' is set to 'Administrators, NT SERVICE\WdiServiceHost'
failure_scenario: An authenticated user with standard privileges can monitor system performance, potentially identifying critical processes or security tools to target.
severity_rationale: Performance monitoring does not directly grant access or take down services, but provides information useful for targeting specific processes or avoiding security tools.

rule_title: 2.2.35 Ensure 'Replace a process level token' is set to 'LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE'
failure_scenario: An authenticated local user with the Replace a process level token privilege can start processes as other users, potentially hiding unauthorized actions and escalating privileges.
severity_rationale: This sensitive privilege allows authenticated local users to impersonate other users and hide their actions, potentially leading to unauthorized access and privilege escalation.

rule_title: 2.2.36 Ensure 'Restore files and directories' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: A non-administrator user with the Restore files and directories privilege can overwrite critical system files or restore sensitive data, potentially compromising system integrity or confidentiality.
severity_rationale: This sensitive privilege allows bypassing file permissions to restore data, which could lead to system compromise or data loss.

rule_title: 2.2.37 Ensure 'Shut down the system' is set to 'Administrators, Users'
failure_scenario: Unauthorized local users can shut down the system, causing a denial-of-service condition.
severity_rationale: Local users can cause a denial-of-service by shutting down the system without requiring elevated privileges.

rule_title: 2.2.38 Ensure 'Take ownership of files or other objects' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: A local user with standard privileges can take ownership of system files, potentially modifying or deleting critical system components.
severity_rationale: This sensitive privilege allows a standard user to bypass all file system permissions, potentially causing system integrity compromise or denial of service.

rule_title: 2.2.4 Ensure 'Adjust memory quotas for a process' is set to 'Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE'
failure_scenario: An unprivileged local user can reduce memory quotas for critical system processes, causing performance degradation or denial of service for business applications.
severity_rationale: Local unprivileged users can degrade system performance or cause service failures by reducing memory quotas for critical processes.

rule_title: 2.2.5 Ensure 'Allow log on locally' is set to 'Administrators, Users'
failure_scenario: Unauthorized local users can log on to the system console, potentially downloading and executing malicious software to elevate privileges.
severity_rationale: Permitting arbitrary local logon grants interactive access to the system, creating full system compromise potential.

rule_title: 2.2.6 Ensure 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services' is set to 'Administrators, Remote Desktop Users'
failure_scenario: Unauthorized users can establish Remote Desktop sessions to the host, gaining unauthorized interactive access to the system.
severity_rationale: Permitting network logon grants interactive access to arbitrary network users with no privileges required, creating full system compromise potential.

rule_title: 2.2.7 Ensure 'Back up files and directories' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: Non-administrator users can bypass file permissions to create unauthorized backups of sensitive system files, potentially exposing encrypted or restricted data.
severity_rationale: Local users can bypass file permissions to create unauthorized backups, potentially exposing sensitive data.

rule_title: 2.2.8 Ensure 'Change the system time' is set to 'Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE'
failure_scenario: An authenticated local user can modify the system time, causing event log timestamps to become inaccurate and potentially disrupting Kerberos authentication and Group Policy application.
severity_rationale: While this doesn't directly grant attacker access or take down services, it weakens system integrity by allowing manipulation of time-based security mechanisms.

rule_title: 2.2.9 Ensure 'Create a pagefile' is set to 'Administrators'
failure_scenario: A local user can reduce the pagefile size to a dangerously small value, causing severe system performance degradation and potential system instability.
severity_rationale: While this doesn't directly grant attacker access or compromise data, it enables a local user to degrade system performance through legitimate configuration changes.

rule_title: 2.3.10.1 Ensure 'Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An authenticated local user can translate the well-known Administrator SID to the actual account name, enabling targeted password guessing attacks against the renamed Administrator account.
severity_rationale: This control prevents information disclosure of the renamed Administrator account name, which could be used to target password guessing attacks.

rule_title: 2.3.10.10 Ensure 'Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM' is set to 'Administrators: Remote Access: Allow'
failure_scenario: An attacker can enumerate local account names via anonymous SAM-RPC calls, enabling credential stuffing or social engineering attacks.
severity_rationale: Anonymous SAM-RPC enumeration allows network attackers to discover valid account names without authentication, enabling credential guessing and social engineering.

rule_title: 2.3.10.11 Ensure 'Network access: Shares that can be accessed anonymously' is set to 'None'
failure_scenario: Anonymous network users can access and potentially modify shared resources, exposing sensitive data or system files.
severity_rationale: Permitting anonymous access to network shares creates a direct remote attack vector for unauthorized data access and modification.

rule_title: 2.3.10.12 Ensure 'Network access: Sharing and security model for local accounts' is set to 'Classic - local users authenticate as themselves'
failure_scenario: Network logons using local accounts are authenticated as Guest, granting uniform low-privilege access to all shared resources regardless of user identity.
severity_rationale: Forces all network logons to use Guest privileges, reducing access control granularity and potentially exposing sensitive resources to unauthorized users.

rule_title: 2.3.10.2 Ensure 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Anonymous network users can enumerate SAM account names, enabling password guessing or social engineering attacks.
severity_rationale: Anonymous enumeration of account names enables credential stuffing and social engineering attacks without requiring any authentication.

rule_title: 2.3.10.3 Ensure 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Anonymous network users can enumerate SAM accounts and network shares, enabling password guessing and social engineering attacks.
severity_rationale: Anonymous enumeration of accounts and shares provides direct information for credential guessing and social engineering attacks.

rule_title: 2.3.10.4 Ensure 'Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A local user can retrieve cached domain credentials from Credential Manager, potentially enabling credential theft or unauthorized access to network resources.
severity_rationale: Local user can access cached credentials without additional privileges, enabling credential theft and network access.

rule_title: 2.3.10.5 Ensure 'Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Anonymous network users can enumerate system accounts and shared resources, enabling information gathering for credential guessing or social engineering attacks.
severity_rationale: Network enumeration provides information for credential guessing but does not directly grant access or take down services.

rule_title: 2.3.10.6 Ensure 'Network access: Named Pipes that can be accessed anonymously' is set to 'None'
failure_scenario: An anonymous network user can access named pipes with elevated permissions, potentially gaining unauthorized system access.
severity_rationale: Permitting anonymous access to named pipes enables direct network compromise of arbitrary services with no authentication required.

rule_title: 2.3.10.7 Ensure 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths' is configured
failure_scenario: An attacker with network access can query sensitive registry keys containing system configuration information, potentially aiding privilege escalation or lateral movement.
severity_rationale: Network exposure of sensitive registry keys allows remote attackers to query system configuration data without authentication.

rule_title: 2.3.10.8 Ensure 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths and sub-paths' is configured
failure_scenario: An attacker with network access can query sensitive registry keys containing system configuration data, potentially aiding privilege escalation or lateral movement.
severity_rationale: Network access to sensitive registry keys allows attackers to gather system configuration information without authentication, potentially aiding privilege escalation or lateral movement.

rule_title: 2.3.10.9 Ensure 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Anonymous network users can enumerate and potentially access shared resources via null sessions, enabling information gathering and potential lateral movement.
severity_rationale: Null session access allows network attackers to query system information without authentication, which can be used to plan further attacks.

rule_title: 2.3.1.1 Ensure 'Accounts: Block Microsoft accounts' is set to 'Users can't add or log on with Microsoft accounts'
failure_scenario: Users can add and log on with Microsoft accounts, potentially bypassing enterprise identity management controls and compliance requirements.
severity_rationale: Permitting Microsoft accounts allows users to bypass enterprise identity controls, creating potential for unauthorized access and compliance violations.

rule_title: 2.3.11.1 Ensure 'Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Local System services using NTLM authentication revert to NULL sessions instead of using the computer identity, potentially allowing unauthorized access to network resources.
severity_rationale: NULL sessions provide no authentication, but this is a defense-in-depth control that prevents downgrade attacks to unencrypted NTLM authentication.

rule_title: 2.3.11.10 Ensure 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) servers' is set to 'Require NTLMv2 session security, Require 128-bit encryption'
failure_scenario: NTLM authentication traffic is downgraded to weaker protocols or encryption levels, potentially exposing credentials to network eavesdropping or tampering.
severity_rationale: Weakened NTLM security enables credential theft via network-based man-in-the-middle attacks against adjacent systems.

rule_title: 2.3.11.11 Ensure 'Network security: Restrict NTLM: Audit Incoming NTLM Traffic' is set to 'Enable auditing for all accounts'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit incoming NTLM traffic prevents detection of legacy authentication attempts, delaying remediation of outdated protocols and leaving systems vulnerable to NTLM-specific attacks.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 2.3.11.12 Ensure 'Network security: Restrict NTLM: Outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers' is set to 'Audit all' or higher
failure_scenario: Outgoing NTLM authentication traffic is not audited, making it difficult to detect and investigate potential NTLM-based attacks.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 2.3.11.2 Ensure 'Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker can establish an unauthenticated NULL session to the host, potentially enumerating shares and other sensitive information.
severity_rationale: NULL sessions allow network information disclosure without authentication, which is a critical security boundary violation.

rule_title: 2.3.11.3 Ensure 'Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Online identities can authenticate to the system using PKU2U, potentially bypassing centralized authentication controls and enabling unauthorized access.
severity_rationale: Permitting PKU2U authentication allows network attackers to bypass centralized authentication controls and gain access to the system.

rule_title: 2.3.11.4 Ensure 'Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos' is set to 'AES128_HMAC_SHA1, AES256_HMAC_SHA1, Future encryption types'
failure_scenario: Kerberos authentication falls back to weaker RC4_HMAC_MD5 encryption, increasing the risk of credential compromise during network authentication.
severity_rationale: Weaker encryption algorithms enable credential theft during network authentication, which is a direct confidentiality impact.

rule_title: 2.3.11.5 Ensure 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker with local system access can extract LM hashes from the SAM database, facilitating offline password cracking attempts.
severity_rationale: Local system compromise enables direct access to SAM database contents, which contains weak LM hashes that can be cracked offline.

rule_title: 2.3.11.6 Ensure 'Network security: Force logoff when logon hours expire' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A user remains connected to the system outside their authorized logon hours, potentially allowing unauthorized access to network resources.
severity_rationale: Unauthorized network access to resources during invalid logon hours creates full compromise potential for the connected system.

rule_title: 2.3.11.7 Ensure 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' is set to 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM'
failure_scenario: Legacy systems authenticate using weak LM or NTLM protocols, enabling credential theft via network sniffing.
severity_rationale: Permitting weak LM/NTLM authentication enables credential theft via adjacent network sniffing, compromising confidentiality.

rule_title: 2.3.11.8 Ensure 'Network security: LDAP client signing requirements' is set to 'Negotiate signing' or higher
failure_scenario: LDAP client requests are sent unsigned, allowing an attacker to intercept and modify LDAP traffic between the client and server.
severity_rationale: LDAP traffic can be intercepted and modified on the same network segment, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.

rule_title: 2.3.11.9 Ensure 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients' is set to 'Require NTLMv2 session security, Require 128-bit encryption'
failure_scenario: NTLM authentication traffic is downgraded to weaker protocols or encryption, allowing an attacker on the same network to capture and decrypt credentials.
severity_rationale: Weakened NTLM security enables credential theft via man-in-the-middle attacks on the same network segment.

rule_title: 2.3.1.2 Ensure 'Accounts: Guest account status' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Unauthenticated network users can log on as Guest with no password, gaining access to any network resources accessible to the Guest account.
severity_rationale: Enabling the Guest account grants network access to arbitrary users with no authentication, creating full system compromise potential.

rule_title: 2.3.1.3 Ensure 'Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A local account with a blank password can be used to log on to the system from remote network locations, potentially allowing unauthorized access.
severity_rationale: Network logon with blank passwords allows immediate unauthorized access to the system, potentially granting full system compromise.

rule_title: 2.3.1.4 Configure 'Accounts: Rename administrator account'
failure_scenario: The built-in Administrator account remains unchanged, making it an easily identifiable target for brute force attacks and credential stuffing.
severity_rationale: The default Administrator account is a well-known target for credential guessing attacks, which could lead to full system compromise.

rule_title: 2.3.1.5 Configure 'Accounts: Rename guest account'
failure_scenario: An attacker can more easily identify and target the guest account, potentially gaining unauthorized access if the account remains enabled.
severity_rationale: Failing to rename the guest account makes it easier for attackers to identify and target this well-known account, potentially leading to unauthorized access if the account remains enabled.

rule_title: 2.3.15.1 Ensure 'System objects: Require case insensitivity for non-Windows subsystems' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A local POSIX user creates a file with the same name as an existing Windows file using different case, causing file access conflicts and potential data corruption.
severity_rationale: Case sensitivity mismatch creates potential for file access conflicts, but does not directly grant attacker access or take down services.

rule_title: 2.3.15.2 Ensure 'System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g. Symbolic Links)' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Weak default permissions on system objects allow unauthorized local users to manipulate shared system resources, potentially enabling privilege escalation or denial of service.
severity_rationale: Weakened default permissions could allow local users to modify system objects, but exploitation requires specific knowledge of the system object being targeted.

rule_title: 2.3.17.1 Ensure 'User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: The built-in Administrator account is enabled and can be used to bypass UAC prompts, potentially allowing privilege escalation.
severity_rationale: Enabling the built-in Administrator account bypasses UAC protections, allowing local attackers to escalate privileges without user interaction.

rule_title: 2.3.17.2 Ensure 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode' is set to 'Prompt for consent on the secure desktop' or higher
failure_scenario: An elevated administrator session silently executes malicious code without user awareness or consent.
severity_rationale: Missing elevation prompts allows local privilege escalation attacks to execute silently with full system compromise potential.

rule_title: 2.3.17.3 Ensure 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users' is set to 'Automatically deny elevation requests'
failure_scenario: A standard user is prompted for administrative credentials when running an application requiring elevation, potentially allowing a malicious program to bypass UAC and execute with elevated privileges.
severity_rationale: User interaction requirement creates a potential window for social engineering attacks to bypass UAC and gain elevated privileges.

rule_title: 2.3.17.4 Ensure 'User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A malicious application with a trusted shell can install additional components without user consent, potentially bypassing security controls.
severity_rationale: Disabling this control allows a local user to install additional software components without explicit consent, potentially enabling privilege escalation or malware persistence.

rule_title: 2.3.17.5 Ensure 'User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A malicious application installed in an untrusted location can bypass UIPI restrictions and manipulate elevated applications, potentially compromising system integrity.
severity_rationale: UIAccess applications can manipulate elevated processes, but this requires a malicious application in an untrusted location and specific conditions to bypass PKI checks.

rule_title: 2.3.17.6 Ensure 'User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Administrators can execute privileged actions without consent prompts, increasing the risk of privilege escalation and unauthorized system changes.
severity_rationale: Disabling Admin Approval Mode removes a critical security boundary between standard and elevated privileges, enabling straightforward privilege escalation.

rule_title: 2.3.17.7 Ensure 'User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker can spoof the elevation prompt dialog box, tricking an authenticated user into entering their credentials or performing an action that grants elevated privileges.
severity_rationale: User interaction is required for exploitation, but the secure desktop is a defense-in-depth control that prevents credential theft and privilege escalation.

rule_title: 2.3.17.8 Ensure 'User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Legacy applications running with elevated privileges write runtime data to protected system locations, potentially allowing privilege escalation or system corruption.
severity_rationale: While this doesn't directly grant attacker access, it enables privilege escalation through legacy application misbehavior.

rule_title: 2.3.2.1 Ensure 'Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings (Windows Vista or later) to override audit policy category settings' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Audit logs contain excessive noise from overly broad audit categories, making it difficult to identify and investigate security-relevant events.
severity_rationale: Disabling this setting would result in excessive audit log noise, making it harder to identify and investigate security-relevant events.

rule_title: 2.3.2.2 Ensure 'Audit: Shut down system immediately if unable to log security audits' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: The system shuts down unexpectedly when audit log capacity is exceeded, causing availability impact and potential data loss.
severity_rationale: Forcing system shutdowns on audit log overflow creates a denial-of-service vulnerability that can be weaponized by attackers or legitimate users.

rule_title: 2.3.7.2 Ensure 'Interactive logon: Don't display last signed-in' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker with console access can view the last logged-in username, potentially enabling credential guessing or brute-force attacks.
severity_rationale: Disclosure of the last username does not directly grant access, but provides information that could facilitate credential guessing attacks.

rule_title: 2.3.7.3 Ensure 'Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit' is set to '900 or fewer second(s), but not 0'
failure_scenario: An unattended logged-in workstation remains unlocked, allowing an unauthorized individual to hijack the active user session.
severity_rationale: Local console takeover of an active user session without authentication.

rule_title: 2.3.7.4 Configure 'Interactive logon: Message text for users attempting to log on'
failure_scenario: Users are not warned about the consequences of unauthorized access or corporate policy violations during the login process, potentially encouraging malicious activity.
severity_rationale: Missing login banner does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 2.3.7.5 Configure 'Interactive logon: Message title for users attempting to log on'
failure_scenario: A threat actor may attempt to log on to the system without being deterred by a warning message.
severity_rationale: The absence of a warning message does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but it may reduce the likelihood of deterring unauthorized access attempts.

rule_title: 2.3.7.6 Ensure 'Interactive logon: Prompt user to change password before expiration' is set to 'between 5 and 14 days'
failure_scenario: Users are not sufficiently warned of upcoming password expiration, potentially causing accidental lockout or delayed password rotation.
severity_rationale: Insufficient password expiration warnings may cause minor availability impact by preventing users from accessing systems during password change periods.

rule_title: 2.3.7.7 Ensure 'Interactive logon: Smart card removal behavior' is set to 'Lock Workstation' or higher
failure_scenario: A user with a smart card logged in leaves their workstation unattended, allowing an attacker to remove the smart card and access the system without authentication.
severity_rationale: Physical access to an unattended workstation allows immediate console takeover of the active user session without password verification.

rule_title: 2.3.8.1 Ensure 'Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always)' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker on the same network can intercept and modify unsigned SMB traffic, potentially hijacking authenticated sessions or impersonating clients/servers to gain unauthorized access.
severity_rationale: Disabling SMB signing allows session hijacking and man-in-the-middle attacks on adjacent network traffic, but requires an existing authenticated session and specific network conditions.

rule_title: 2.3.8.2 Ensure 'Microsoft network client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Plaintext passwords are transmitted across the network to third-party SMB servers, potentially allowing network eavesdroppers to capture and reuse credentials.
severity_rationale: Network eavesdropping enables credential theft and unauthorized access to third-party SMB services.

rule_title: 2.3.9.1 Ensure 'Microsoft network server: Amount of idle time required before suspending session' is set to '15 or fewer minute(s)'
failure_scenario: An attacker can establish numerous SMB sessions to exhaust server resources, causing performance degradation or denial of service.
severity_rationale: Network attackers can create many idle SMB sessions to exhaust server resources, causing availability impact without requiring authentication or privileges.

rule_title: 2.3.9.2 Ensure 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker on the same network can intercept and modify unsigned SMB traffic, potentially hijacking authenticated sessions or impersonating systems.
severity_rationale: Session hijacking requires specific network conditions and timing, but enables full compromise of authenticated sessions.

rule_title: 2.3.9.3 Ensure 'Microsoft network server: Disconnect clients when logon hours expire' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A user with an expired logon hour session maintains an active SMB connection to the host, potentially allowing continued unauthorized access to network resources.
severity_rationale: Network users with expired logon hours retain active SMB sessions, enabling continued unauthorized access to network resources.

rule_title: 2.3.9.4 Ensure 'Microsoft network server: Server SPN target name validation level' is set to 'Accept if provided by client' or higher
failure_scenario: An attacker can spoof the identity of a legitimate SMB server and relay authentication requests to gain unauthorized access to network resources.
severity_rationale: Failure to validate SPN allows SMB relay attacks, enabling network-level impersonation of legitimate servers and full compromise of network resources.

rule_title: 5.10 Ensure 'LxssManager (LxssManager)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in a Linux application running under WSL to gain local system access, potentially compromising the entire Windows host.
severity_rationale: While WSL provides useful functionality, it creates a potential attack surface for Linux application vulnerabilities to escalate to full system compromise.

rule_title: 5.11 Ensure 'Microsoft FTP Service (FTPSVC)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker exploits the FTP service to gain unauthorized access to files on the system, potentially compromising sensitive data.
severity_rationale: Running an FTP server on a workstation significantly increases the attack surface, allowing remote attackers to potentially access or modify files without authentication.

rule_title: 5.13 Ensure 'OpenSSH SSH Server (sshd)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker gains unauthorized remote access to the workstation via SSH, potentially compromising the system and network.
severity_rationale: Running an SSH server on a workstation creates a direct network attack vector, enabling remote compromise of the system and network.

rule_title: 5.24 Ensure 'Remote Procedure Call (RPC) Locator (RpcLocator)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Legacy applications requiring RPC Locator may fail to function properly, potentially causing application compatibility issues.
severity_rationale: Disabling this legacy service primarily impacts application compatibility rather than security, with minimal availability impact if applications fail to start.

rule_title: 5.26 Ensure 'Routing and Remote Access (RemoteAccess)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker with local administrative privileges can enable the Routing and Remote Access service to create a rogue router, enabling network traffic interception and manipulation.
severity_rationale: This service is inappropriate for workstations and can be weaponized by local administrators to create network attack infrastructure.

rule_title: 5.28 Ensure 'Simple TCP/IP Services (simptcp)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker uses the enabled TCP/IP services to perform network reconnaissance, amplification attacks, or denial of service against other systems.
severity_rationale: Enabled TCP/IP services can be used as network-based attack vectors without authentication or user interaction.

rule_title: 5.3 Ensure 'Computer Browser (Browser)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: The Computer Browser service generates excessive network traffic and shares system information with unauthenticated network peers, potentially aiding network reconnaissance.
severity_rationale: The service generates unnecessary network traffic and shares system information with unauthenticated peers, potentially aiding network reconnaissance.

rule_title: 5.30 Ensure 'Special Administration Console Helper (sacsvr)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker with network access can remotely execute commands on the system via the Emergency Management Services console.
severity_rationale: This service provides remote command execution with administrative privileges, creating full system compromise potential if enabled.

rule_title: 5.31 Ensure 'SSDP Discovery (SSDPSRV)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Automatic SSDP discovery and announcement enables unauthorized network devices to connect to the host, potentially exposing services or allowing remote code execution.
severity_rationale: SSDP discovery enables automatic network service attachment, which is a significant security risk in enterprise environments.

rule_title: 5.32 Ensure 'UPnP Device Host (upnphost)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker can discover and exploit UPnP services on the host, potentially gaining unauthorized access or executing arbitrary commands.
severity_rationale: UPnP service discovery and automatic connection establishment create a direct network attack surface for remote exploitation.

rule_title: 5.33 Ensure 'Web Management Service (WMSvc)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker remotely exploits the Web Management Service to gain administrative access to the IIS web server and underlying system.
severity_rationale: The Web Management Service provides remote administrative access to IIS and the underlying system, creating a significant attack surface for network-based attackers.

rule_title: 5.36 Ensure 'Windows Media Player Network Sharing Service (WMPNetworkSvc)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker on the local network can discover and access shared media libraries from the host, potentially leaking sensitive content.
severity_rationale: Network sharing of media files may expose sensitive content to adjacent network devices without authentication.

rule_title: 5.37 Ensure 'Windows Mobile Hotspot Service (icssvc)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker with physical access to a domain-connected workstation can enable the mobile hotspot service to create an unsecured wireless access point, exposing internal network resources to unauthorized users.
severity_rationale: Physical access allows immediate compromise of internal network resources through an unsecured wireless access point.

rule_title: 5.41 Ensure 'World Wide Web Publishing Service (W3SVC)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker exploits a web application vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to the system hosting the web server.
severity_rationale: Running a web server on a workstation significantly increases the attack surface and creates a direct network entry point for attackers to exploit web application vulnerabilities.

rule_title: 5.42 Ensure 'Xbox Accessory Management Service (XboxGipSvc)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: The Xbox Accessory Management Service remains running, potentially exposing the system to unauthorized access through connected Xbox accessories.
severity_rationale: While the Xbox Accessory Management Service is not directly exploitable, leaving it enabled represents an unnecessary risk in enterprise environments.

rule_title: 5.43 Ensure 'Xbox Live Auth Manager (XblAuthManager)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Xbox Live Auth Manager service remains running, potentially exposing the system to unauthorized access or data exfiltration through Xbox Live network services.
severity_rationale: Running unauthorized Xbox Live services creates a network attack surface for potential compromise of the system.

rule_title: 5.44 Ensure 'Xbox Live Game Save (XblGameSave)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: The Xbox Live Game Save service remains running, potentially exposing user gaming data to unauthorized cloud synchronization.
severity_rationale: While not directly enabling system compromise, this service could expose gaming data to unintended recipients, violating data protection policies.

rule_title: 5.45 Ensure 'Xbox Live Networking Service (XboxNetApiSvc)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: The Xbox Live Networking Service remains running, potentially exposing the system to unauthorized network connections and data exfiltration.
severity_rationale: The service creates a network connection to Xbox Live servers, which may be exploited for data exfiltration or unauthorized access.

rule_title: 5.6 Ensure 'IIS Admin Service (IISADMIN)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker with local access to a workstation running IIS can manipulate the metabase configuration, potentially compromising the web server or enabling further attacks.
severity_rationale: Local user with IIS Admin Service access can modify web server configuration, potentially leading to full system compromise.

rule_title: 5.7 Ensure 'Infrared monitor service (irmon)' is set to 'Disabled' or 'Not Installed'
failure_scenario: An attacker with a nearby infrared device can trigger the automatic file transfer application, potentially exfiltrating sensitive data.
severity_rationale: Infrared communication is inherently insecure and can be exploited from the same physical proximity without authentication.

rule_title: 5.8 Ensure 'Internet Connection Sharing (ICS) (SharedAccess)' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: ICS creates an unsecured network bridge between the internal and external network interfaces, potentially exposing internal systems to external threats.
severity_rationale: ICS creates a network bridge that bypasses enterprise security controls, potentially exposing internal systems to external threats.

rule_title: 9.2.1 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Firewall state' is set to 'On (recommended)'
failure_scenario: The system's built-in Private Firewall is disabled, allowing unrestricted network access to all services and potentially enabling remote exploitation of vulnerabilities.
severity_rationale: Disabling the Private Firewall removes all network-based access controls, creating a direct path for remote exploitation of any network-facing vulnerabilities.

rule_title: 9.2.2 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Inbound connections' is set to 'Block (default)'
failure_scenario: A remote attacker exploits a vulnerable network service to gain unauthorized access to the system.
severity_rationale: Permitting all inbound traffic allows remote exploitation of any network service vulnerabilities without additional firewall rules.

rule_title: 9.2.3 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Settings: Display a notification' is set to 'No'
failure_scenario: Users are presented with confusing firewall notifications that they cannot resolve, potentially causing them to ignore security warnings.
severity_rationale: This is a user experience control with no direct security impact; notifications may cause users to ignore legitimate security warnings.

rule_title: 9.2.4 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Logging: Name' is configured
failure_scenario: Windows Firewall logs are not written to a dedicated file, making it difficult to identify and analyze private network firewall events during security incidents.
severity_rationale: Missing dedicated firewall logs weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails for private network traffic.

rule_title: 9.2.5 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Logging: Size limit (KB)' is set to '16,384 KB or greater'
failure_scenario: Windows Firewall logs are truncated before reaching the end of the log file, potentially obscuring forensic evidence of security incidents.
severity_rationale: Insufficient log size limits weaken the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails, potentially obscuring forensic evidence.

rule_title: 9.2.6 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Logging: Log dropped packets' is set to 'Yes'
failure_scenario: Failure to log dropped packets impedes forensic investigation and intrusion detection during security incidents, delaying threat response.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 9.2.7 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Logging: Log successful connections' is set to 'Yes'
failure_scenario: Failure to log successful connections impedes forensic investigation and incident response by obscuring legitimate network activity.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 9.3.1 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Public: Firewall state' is set to 'On (recommended)'
failure_scenario: The system's public network interface is unprotected, allowing unrestricted inbound and outbound network traffic, potentially enabling remote exploitation of network services.
severity_rationale: Disabling the public firewall removes all network-based access controls, creating a direct path for remote exploitation of any network-facing vulnerabilities.

rule_title: 9.3.2 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Public: Inbound connections' is set to 'Block (default)'
failure_scenario: An attacker can remotely exploit unpatched network services on the host due to the firewall not blocking all inbound connections by default.
severity_rationale: Network attackers can immediately exploit any unpatched network services without requiring local access or user interaction.

rule_title: 9.3.3 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Public: Settings: Display a notification' is set to 'No
failure_scenario: Firewall blocks legitimate network traffic without user notification, causing connectivity issues that may be misdiagnosed as network problems.
severity_rationale: Disabling notifications does not directly enable attacks, but may cause availability issues when legitimate traffic is blocked by firewall rules.

rule_title: 9.3.4 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Public: Logging: Name' is configured
failure_scenario: Windows Firewall events are not recorded to a dedicated log file, making it difficult to analyze system issues or unauthorized activities.
severity_rationale: Missing dedicated firewall logs weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails, but does not directly grant attacker access or take down services.

rule_title: 9.3.5 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Public: Logging: Size limit (KB)' is set to '16,384 KB or greater'
failure_scenario: Windows Firewall logs are truncated due to insufficient log file size, potentially obscuring security events and making forensic analysis difficult.
severity_rationale: Insufficient log size does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 9.3.6 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Public: Logging: Log dropped packets' is set to 'Yes'
failure_scenario: Failure to log dropped packets in public network profiles impedes forensic investigation and intrusion detection during security incidents, delaying threat response.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 9.3.7 Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Public: Logging: Log successful connections' is set to 'Yes'
failure_scenario: Failure to log successful connections impedes forensic investigation and incident response during security incidents, delaying threat detection.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 1.1.1 Ensure 'Enforce password history' is set to '24 or more password(s)'
failure_scenario: A user can reuse a small number of passwords, increasing the risk of brute force attacks and credential compromise.
severity_rationale: Limiting password reuse reduces the window for brute force attacks and credential compromise, but the impact is primarily on authentication integrity rather than direct system compromise.

rule_title: 1.1.2 Ensure 'Maximum password age' is set to '365 or fewer days, but not 0'
failure_scenario: A compromised password remains valid for an extended period, increasing the window of opportunity for unauthorized access.
severity_rationale: Passwords with unlimited validity enable indefinite credential reuse, creating a persistent attack surface for credential theft and reuse.

rule_title: 1.1.3 Ensure 'Minimum password age' is set to '1 or more day(s)'
failure_scenario: A user can immediately change their password to a previously used password, potentially reusing a compromised password.
severity_rationale: Allows rapid password cycling to bypass password history enforcement, potentially reusing compromised passwords.

rule_title: 1.1.4 Ensure 'Minimum password length' is set to '14 or more character(s)'
failure_scenario: Weak passwords of 13 characters or fewer enable brute force or dictionary attacks to compromise user accounts.
severity_rationale: Network attackers can easily brute force or guess short passwords to gain unauthorized access to user accounts.

rule_title: 1.1.5 Ensure 'Password must meet complexity requirements' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Weak passwords are allowed, making them vulnerable to brute force and dictionary attacks, potentially leading to unauthorized access.
severity_rationale: Weak passwords enable straightforward credential guessing attacks that could lead to full system compromise.

rule_title: 1.1.6 Ensure 'Relax minimum password length limits' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Local accounts are limited to weak passwords of 14 characters or less, increasing the risk of brute force or dictionary attacks.
severity_rationale: Weak local passwords enable credential guessing attacks against local accounts, which could lead to full system compromise.

rule_title: 1.1.7 Ensure 'Store passwords using reversible encryption' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker with access to the system's SAM database or Active Directory can retrieve plaintext user passwords, enabling unauthorized access to systems and services.
severity_rationale: Reversible encryption storage of passwords creates a direct path to credential compromise for attackers with local system access.

rule_title: 1.2.1 Ensure 'Account lockout duration' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
failure_scenario: A local attacker can lock out legitimate user accounts by repeatedly attempting to log in with incorrect credentials, causing temporary denial of service.
severity_rationale: Account lockout is a defense-in-depth control; failing to implement it does not directly grant attacker access, but creates a denial-of-service vector against legitimate users.

rule_title: 1.2.2 Ensure 'Account lockout threshold' is set to '5 or fewer invalid logon attempt(s), but not 0'
failure_scenario: An attacker can perform an online brute force password guessing attack against a domain user account without risk of account lockout.
severity_rationale: Disabling account lockout enables indefinite online password guessing attempts, which could lead to account compromise.

rule_title: 1.2.3 Ensure 'Allow Administrator account lockout' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: The built-in Administrator account remains unlocked after repeated failed login attempts, enabling brute force password guessing attacks.
severity_rationale: Disabling account lockout for the built-in Administrator account creates a persistent credential brute force target with full system compromise potential.

rule_title: 1.2.4 Ensure 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
failure_scenario: An attacker can repeatedly attempt to authenticate to multiple accounts, triggering lockouts and disrupting legitimate user access.
severity_rationale: Network attackers can cause availability disruption by triggering account lockouts, but cannot directly compromise confidentiality or integrity.

rule_title: 17.1.1 Ensure 'Audit Credential Validation' is set to 'Success and Failure'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit credential validation events prevents detection of credential theft, brute force attacks, or unauthorized logon attempts.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.2.2 Ensure 'Audit Security Group Management' is set to include 'Success'

rule_title: 17.2.3 Ensure 'Audit User Account Management' is set to 'Success and Failure'

rule_title: 17.3.2 Ensure 'Audit Process Creation' is set to include 'Success'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit process creation events weakens forensic investigation capabilities and incident response effectiveness.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.5.1 Ensure 'Audit Account Lockout' is set to include 'Failure'
failure_scenario: Account lockout events are not logged, making it difficult to detect and investigate brute force or credential stuffing attacks.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.5.2 Ensure 'Audit Group Membership' is set to include 'Success'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit successful group membership changes may obscure legitimate privilege escalation or lateral movement activity during an attack.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.5.3 Ensure 'Audit Logoff' is set to include 'Success'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit successful logoffs prevents tracking of user session termination events, complicating forensic analysis of user activity.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.5.4 Ensure 'Audit Logon' is set to 'Success and Failure'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit logon events makes it difficult to detect and investigate unauthorized access attempts or successful logons, weakening forensic capabilities.
severity_rationale: Missing logon audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.5.5 Ensure 'Audit Other Logon/Logoff Events' is set to 'Success and Failure'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit logon/logoff events may obscure critical security events during forensic analysis, potentially delaying incident response.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.5.6 Ensure 'Audit Special Logon' is set to include 'Success'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit special logon events obscures potential privilege escalation attempts, complicating forensic investigation and compliance reporting.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.6.1 Ensure 'Audit Detailed File Share' is set to include 'Failure'
failure_scenario: Unauthorized access attempts to network shares are not logged, making it difficult to detect and investigate potential intrusions.
severity_rationale: Missing audit logs does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 17.6.2 Ensure 'Audit File Share' is set to 'Success and Failure'
failure_scenario: Failure to audit file share access events may obscure malicious activity or unauthorized data exfiltration from workstations.

rule_title: 17.6.3 Ensure 'Audit Other Object Access Events' is set to 'Success and Failure'

rule_title: 18.10.13.1 Ensure 'Turn off cloud consumer account state content' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A user signs into a workstation using a personal Microsoft account, potentially exposing enterprise data to unauthorized cloud services.
severity_rationale: User interaction is required to connect a personal account, but this creates a potential data leakage path to consumer cloud services.

rule_title: 18.10.13.3 Ensure 'Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: Third-party apps silently install and run on the system, potentially sending data back to third-party servers without user consent.
severity_rationale: Silent third-party app installation and execution creates potential data exfiltration and system integrity risks.

rule_title: 18.10.14.1 Ensure 'Require pin for pairing' is set to 'Enabled: First Time' OR 'Enabled: Always'
failure_scenario: An attacker can pair a malicious wireless display device to the system without a PIN, potentially intercepting or manipulating the display output.
severity_rationale: Adjacent network attackers can intercept or manipulate display output without authentication, compromising confidentiality and integrity of displayed information.

rule_title: 18.10.15.1 Ensure 'Do not display the password reveal button' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker with visual access to the user's screen can observe password entry and potentially capture credentials.
severity_rationale: Physical observation of password entry enables credential theft without technical interaction.

rule_title: 18.10.15.2 Ensure 'Enumerate administrator accounts on elevation' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An authenticated local user can enumerate administrator accounts during privilege escalation attempts, potentially aiding credential cracking efforts.
severity_rationale: Disclosure of administrator accounts does not directly grant access or take down services, but provides information that could aid credential guessing attacks.

rule_title: 18.10.15.3 Ensure 'Prevent the use of security questions for local accounts' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker can reset a local user's password by answering security questions that were easily guessed or discovered from the user's social media activity.
severity_rationale: Security questions provide weak authentication that can be bypassed with social engineering or information gathering.

rule_title: 18.10.16.1 Ensure 'Allow Diagnostic Data' is set to 'Enabled: Diagnostic data off (not recommended)' or 'Enabled: Send required diagnostic data'
failure_scenario: Sending optional diagnostic data to Microsoft may expose sensitive system information and user activity patterns, potentially violating privacy policies.
severity_rationale: Sending optional diagnostic data exposes sensitive system information and user activity patterns, potentially violating privacy policies and creating a data leakage risk.

rule_title: 18.10.16.3 Ensure 'Do not show feedback notifications' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: User feedback notifications are displayed, potentially exposing sensitive system information to Microsoft without explicit consent.
severity_rationale: While not directly exploitable, this setting violates data protection principles by enabling unauthorized data sharing with Microsoft.

rule_title: 18.10.17.1 Ensure 'Download Mode' is NOT set to 'Enabled: Internet'
failure_scenario: Windows Update downloads are shared with untrusted peers on the Internet, potentially exposing sensitive update content to malicious actors.
severity_rationale: Internet peering enables unauthorized network users to observe Windows Update traffic, potentially disclosing sensitive system information.

rule_title: 18.10.18.2 Ensure 'Enable App Installer Experimental Features' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: A local user enables experimental features in the Windows Package Manager, potentially installing unstable or untested software packages.
severity_rationale: Enabling experimental features could introduce instability or security vulnerabilities, but does not directly grant attacker access or take down services.

rule_title: 18.10.18.3 Ensure 'Enable App Installer Hash Override' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: A local user can bypass SHA256 validation for package installation, potentially installing malicious software.
severity_rationale: Allows local users to bypass critical package integrity validation, enabling installation of potentially malicious software.

rule_title: 18.10.18.4 Ensure 'Enable App Installer Local Archive Malware Scan Override' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An authenticated local user can bypass Windows Defender malware scanning when installing software from local archives, potentially installing malicious applications.
severity_rationale: Local users can bypass malware scanning when installing software from local archives, potentially installing malicious applications.

rule_title: 18.10.18.5 Ensure 'Enable App Installer Microsoft Store Source Certificate Validation Bypass' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: An attacker can spoof the Microsoft Store source, potentially delivering malicious packages to the system.
severity_rationale: Certificate validation bypass allows potential spoofing of the Microsoft Store source, which could lead to the installation of malicious packages, but requires a complex attack scenario.

rule_title: 18.10.18.6 Ensure 'Enable App Installer ms-appinstaller protocol' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: A user clicks a malicious ms-appinstaller link, installing unauthorized software on the system.
severity_rationale: User interaction with malicious links enables full system compromise without requiring elevated privileges.

rule_title: 18.10.26.1.1 Ensure 'Application: Control Event Log behavior when the log file reaches its maximum size' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Event logs are overwritten when full, potentially obscuring evidence of security incidents or system problems.
severity_rationale: Log overwriting does not directly grant attacker access or take down services, but weakens the integrity of security monitoring and audit trails.

rule_title: 18.10.26.1.2 Ensure 'Application: Specify the maximum log file size (KB)' is set to 'Enabled: 32,768 or greater'
failure_scenario: Security event logs are overwritten by excessive volume of events, potentially obscuring evidence of security incidents or unauthorized activity.
severity_rationale: Limited log retention reduces the integrity of forensic evidence, though an attacker would need to generate sufficient events to overwrite logs.

rule_title: 18.10.26.2.1 Ensure 'Security: Control Event Log behavior when the log file reaches its maximum size' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Event logs are overwritten when full, potentially obscuring evidence of security incidents or system problems.
severity_rationale: Log overwriting weakens forensic capabilities but does not directly grant attacker access or take down services.

rule_title: 18.10.26.2.2 Ensure 'Security: Specify the maximum log file size (KB)' is set to 'Enabled: 196,608 or greater'
failure_scenario: Security event logs are overwritten by excessive events, potentially obscuring evidence of security incidents or unauthorized access.
severity_rationale: Limited log retention enables attackers to cover their tracks by generating excessive events, though this requires elevated privileges to clear logs.

rule_title: 18.10.26.3.1 Ensure 'Setup: Control Event Log behavior when the log file reaches its maximum size' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Event logs are overwritten when full, potentially obscuring evidence of security incidents or system problems.
severity_rationale: Log overwriting weakens forensic capabilities but does not directly grant attacker access or take down services.

rule_title: 18.10.26.3.2 Ensure 'Setup: Specify the maximum log file size (KB)' is set to 'Enabled: 32,768 or greater'
failure_scenario: Event logs are overwritten by excessive system events, obscuring security-relevant events and making forensic investigation difficult.
severity_rationale: Limited log retention reduces the integrity of audit trails, though direct system compromise is not enabled.

rule_title: 18.10.26.4.1 Ensure 'System: Control Event Log behavior when the log file reaches its maximum size' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Event logs are overwritten when full, potentially obscuring evidence of security incidents or system problems.
severity_rationale: Log overwriting weakens forensic capabilities but does not directly grant attacker access or take down services.

rule_title: 18.10.26.4.2 Ensure 'System: Specify the maximum log file size (KB)' is set to 'Enabled: 32,768 or greater'
failure_scenario: Security event logs are overwritten by excessive events, potentially obscuring evidence of security incidents or unauthorized access.
severity_rationale: A privileged attacker could clear logs, but the primary risk is that legitimate security events are lost due to log rotation, weakening forensic capabilities.

rule_title: 18.10.29.3 Ensure 'Turn off Data Execution Prevention for Explorer' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Legacy plug-in applications that require DEP exceptions may fail to function properly, potentially causing system instability or security vulnerabilities.
severity_rationale: Disabling DEP for Explorer may cause application failures, but does not directly enable exploitation of vulnerabilities.

rule_title: 18.10.29.4 Ensure 'Do not apply the Mark of the Web tag to files copied from insecure sources' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Files downloaded from untrusted sources are not tagged with Mark of the Web, potentially exposing users to security risks when opening these files.
severity_rationale: Disabling MOTW tags reduces the security warnings for files from untrusted sources, but does not directly enable exploitation without user interaction.

rule_title: 18.10.29.5 Ensure 'Turn off heap termination on corruption' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Legacy plug-in applications continue functioning after a File Explorer session becomes corrupt, potentially allowing an attacker to maintain persistence or escalate privileges.
severity_rationale: While heap termination is a defense-in-depth control, failing to terminate on corruption may allow an attacker to maintain persistence or escalate privileges in specific scenarios.

rule_title: 18.10.29.6 Ensure 'Turn off shell protocol protected mode' is set to 'Disabled'
failure_scenario: Applications can open arbitrary folders and launch files through the shell protocol, increasing the attack surface for local privilege escalation.
severity_rationale: Disabling protected mode reduces the attack surface for local privilege escalation by limiting shell protocol functionality to a restricted set of operations.

rule_title: 18.10.41.1 Ensure 'Block all consumer Microsoft account user authentication' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A user can authenticate to the system using a consumer Microsoft account, bypassing corporate identity management controls.
severity_rationale: This control prevents Microsoft account authentication, which may bypass corporate identity management policies, but does not directly grant attacker access or take down services.

rule_title: 18.10.4.2 Ensure 'Not allow per-user unsigned packages to install by default (requires explicitly allow per install)' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: An authenticated local user can install unsigned Windows App packages without explicit IT approval, potentially introducing malicious software.
severity_rationale: Local users can install unsigned packages without IT oversight, potentially introducing malware or unauthorized software.

rule_title: 18.10.4.3 Ensure 'Prevent non-admin users from installing packaged Windows apps' is set to 'Enabled'
failure_scenario: A non-administrator user can install unapproved Windows app packages, potentially introducing malicious software or unauthorized applications.
